row.cell:
Consider the following integral. Sketch its region of integration in the xy-plane. \displaystyle \int_{-2}^{0} \int_{-\sqrt{4 - x^2}}^{0} 4xy \, dy \, dx (a) Which graph shows the region of integration in the xy-plane?
?
A
B
C
D
(b) Evaluate the integral.

cell.p: (Click on a graph to enlarge it)

solution.p: (a) The region is bounded below by y= - \sqrt{4 -x^2 }, which represents the lower part of a circle centered at the origin and of radius 2, and above by y = 0. Since -2 \le x \le 0, the region represents the quarter of a disk in the third quadrant and it matches graph C.

p.m: \begin{array}{lcl} \displaystyle \int_{-2}^{0} \int_{-\sqrt{4 - x^2}}^{0} 4xy \, dy \, dx \amp =\amp \displaystyle 4 \int_{-2}^0 x \left[\frac{y^2}{2} \right]_{- \sqrt{4 -x^2 }}^0 \, dx \\ \amp =\amp \displaystyle - 2 \int_{-2}^0 x (4-x^2) \, dx \\ \amp =\amp \displaystyle -2 \left[ 4 \frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^4}{4} \right]_{-2}^0 \\ \amp = \amp \displaystyle -2 \left( \frac{2^4}{4} - \frac{2^4}{2} \right) \\ \amp =\amp 8 \end{array}
